methods.label: Disprove both identities with one pair
methods.explanation: An even function must satisfy \(f(-x)=f(x)\) for every real \(x\), while an odd function must satisfy \(f(-x)=-f(x)\). A single failed pair can rule out both: \(f(1)=2\) and \(f(-1)=0\). Since \(0\ne2\) and \(0\ne-2\), the function is neither odd nor even, choice A.
